1.explanation: We use the Lighthouse Node API and Chrome Launcher to programmatically reproduce the NO_TTI_CPU_IDLE_PERIOD error. By passing throttlingMethod='provided' we simulate exactly the DevTools path. The Glitch URL parameter delayFcpMs=1700 holds off FCP by ~1.7 s, then does almost no work – so Lighthouse finds no “quiet window” after FCP before trace end and throws the NO_TTI_CPU_IDLE_PERIOD error for both TTI and TBT.
1.bug_scenario: When you navigate to a page that artificially delays its First Contentful Paint (FCP) by ~1.7 s and then does almost no work afterwards, Lighthouse (with “provided” / DevTools throttling) will throw NO_TTI_CPU_IDLE_PERIOD for both Time to Interactive (TTI) and Total Blocking Time (TBT). In the screenshot you can see FCP reported at ~2.3 s, Speed Index at ~1 s, Largest Contentful Paint at ~2.3 s—all green—but both TTI and TBT show “Error! (NO_TTI_CPU_IDLE_PERIOD)”.
